written.myAnswer: Consistency of results means obtaining similar results when measurements are repeated.

A systematic error is a consistent error that shifts measurements in the same direction, often due to an instrument or method; it can be corrected by applying a constant adjustment. A random error causes measurements to vary unpredictably from one reading to another.
Random errors result from unpredictable changes during an experiment, such as instrument limitations, environmental factors, or slight variations in procedure.
Yes. A systematic error affects the accuracy of a measurement.

Accuracy is how close a measurement is to the actual value. Precision is how close repeated measurements are to one another. Systematic error affects accuracy, while random error often affects precision.
Correct systematic errors by applying the appropriate constant adjustment to each measurement.
Yes. Measurements can be inaccurate if they are not close to the actual value and imprecise if they are not close to one another.
